correctness.rationale: For state zero the probability of an upward jump is floor(K eta b)/K; for state one the probability of a downward jump is ceil(K eta(1-b))/K. Since 0<eta<1 the sum is in (0,1], so solving two-state balance gives a unique invariant distribution and its finite-time convergence. The ideal kernel has upward and downward rates eta b, eta(1-b), hence invariant Bernoulli(b). The normalized error b-floor(vb)/(floor(vb)+ceil(v(1-b))) is nonnegative. Writing v=n+theta, vb=k+u, the rate denominator is n+1 when u<theta and n when u>=theta. Both cases bound the error by 1/v; targets b increasing to 1/v from below attain that upper bound as a supremum. If v<=1 the chain is absorbed at zero and errors approach one. The bit-budget condition follows exactly. The executable verifies 41,776 exact-rational cases but is supplementary to the proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 StochasticA survey defines the floor-based finite-random-bit probability but provides no invariant-law or minimax bit-budget theorem; Fitzgibbon-Felix 2025 calculate one-round bias and correct it, not the stationary amplification. El Arar et al. 2024/2025 study stochastic rounding and finite-horizon bounds, including empirical gradient descent, not this sharp two-state invariant. Li et al. 2017 analyze ideally rounded quantized Markov training; their stationary-limit theorem assumes stochastic gradients with both positive and negative support and does not treat truncated random thresholds. Xia et al. 2023 consider distinct exact stochastic fixed-point rounding models. A previous numerical summation absorption result uses repeated positive additions on a floating point binade, not a two-state gradient stationary law. None of those statements implies the combined exact floor/ceiling invariant mass, sharp min(1,1/(K eta)) supremum, and if-and-only-if random-bit scale. Universal historical-priority proof is not claimed.
residual_risks: The search cannot establish global historical priority. Other finite-state quantized optimization or stochastic rounding treatments may imply this exact special-case envelope.

The result is a minimal two-level fixed-point model and should not be extrapolated to floating-point binades, high-dimensional training, stochastic gradients, or corrected/nearest-based stochastic rounding.

value.rationale: The invariant probability is a natural long-run accuracy invariant for a repeatedly quantized optimizer. Its target-uniform total-variation difference from an ideal stochastic-rounding chain directly measures damage from finite random-bit budget. The sharp threshold K eta<=1 produces universal absorption at one endpoint despite strongly convex real drift; above it the exact minimax error is 1/(K eta), proving that fixed learning-rate-scaled bit budgets are insufficient for uniform small-step fidelity. The iff asymptotic and exact prescribed-tolerance bit count specify an operational resource law that finite-time average rounding-bias estimates do not supply. This is a complete motivated classification on the smallest nontrivial quantization cell, not a numerical curiosity chosen after calculating unrelated parameters.
